title: Dist Bs 1 — three gated bass notes
method: Inspected raw librarian patch parameters against Roland MIDI Implementation map. No engine synthesis parameters were optimized. Decoded official MP3 to stereo44.1kHz16-bit PCM; used channel mean for pitch and gating analysis. Detected six amplitude gates from4ms RMS of a100Hz high-pass analysis signal with10–50milliFS thresholds; threshold variation typically<6ms. Onset/gate intervals padded in uncertainty for MP3 and filter response. Confirmed sounding MIDI27 and29 using harmonic spectra and90ms-window autocorrelation; adding36 semitones reverses the documented oscillator coarse tune in both tones. Gate-on/off estimates do not distinguish silent keyboard onset from recording latency or encoded pre-echo.
uncertainties: Three-note crop from 1.94–3.20 seconds of the original demo; the earlier note with obvious pitch movement is outside this excerpt.
Notes 63, 63, 65 are inferred from hardware fundamentals and the unchanged preset oscillator tuning. Onsets have approximately 10 ms and note-offs 12 ms uncertainty.
All velocities are fixed to 100, an unknown placeholder. Both tones have amplitude velocity sensitivity +8.
Original MIDI, controller events, system tuning/transposition, gain and processing are unavailable; no waveform null or absolute loudness calibration is justified.
Septum starts from reset; hardware was already sounding earlier in the recording. The crop begins in a quiet gap, with preset delay and reverb disabled.
